what_it_does: Presto is a chip that enables a powerful but computationally expensive cryptographic technique called fully homomorphic encryption (FHE)—a method that lets you run calculations on data while it stays encrypted, so servers never see the raw information. The problem is that FHE is thousands of times slower than normal computation. Presto combines a general-purpose processor core (a RISC-V CPU) with specialized hardware that accelerates the specific math operations at the heart of FHE: polynomial multiplications (done via a fast algorithm called NTT) and operations on special mathematical structures called module lattices. It supports multiple FHE schemes, letting applications choose the right tradeoff between security and speed.
